name: complete-reacto-star
transcript:
Interviewer: Walk me through the problem.
Candidate: I need two distinct indices whose values sum to the target. For [2,7,11,15] and 9, I return [0,1]; duplicates such as [3,3] must work. I will scan once and store prior values by index, which is linear time and linear space.
Candidate: I expect the ordinary and duplicate cases to pass.
Interviewer: Tell me about a debugging disagreement.
Candidate: On a release, I owned a failing cache test. I reproduced it, proposed invalidation on writes, and paired with my teammate to test it. The incidents stopped in the following releases.

name: out-of-order-complete-reacto
transcript: Candidate: I will use a one-pass map in linear time. Before coding, [3,3] with target 6 should return both distinct positions. Restating the goal, I return indices, not values. After coding I would also test a negative target; the approach is already asymptotically optimal.

name: failed-test-recovery
transcript: Candidate: The duplicate case failed because I inserted before checking and reused one index. I will reverse those operations and rerun it.

name: skipped-star
transcript: Candidate: I am finishing the implementation and checking the duplicate case now.

name: star-we-without-personal-action
transcript:
Interviewer: Tell me about a production bug your team handled.
Candidate: We had an outage and we fixed it quickly. The service recovered.

name: star-qualitative-result
transcript:
Interviewer: Tell me about learning from a mistake.
Candidate: During a migration I owned the rollout checklist but missed a rollback check. I added a dry-run review and practiced it with the team. We had no numeric metric, but later migrations had a clear rollback owner and the team caught mistakes before deployment.
